atoms.text: For each of the main five religions, there are different types of buildings of worship. Many of these buildings are visited regularly by people who pray and celebrate their religion. Over time, building styles have changed, so some buildings are old-fashioned while others are modern.

The Muslim building of worship is called a mosque. Something unique about mosques is that during service, worshippers always face towards Mecca, which is the most holy place in the world for Muslims. Christians celebrate their religion in churches and often face an altar with a cross above it during their service.

People who practice Judaism go to synagogues. Like all religious buildings, synagogues can look very different from one another, but nearly all have an ark - a special place where the Torah is kept. Both people who are Hindu and people who are Buddhist celebrate in buildings called temples.
